beats.say: Some of these sharks were born before the United States existed.
Deep in the freezing Arctic, it cruises in the dark.

It grows about one centimeter a year.
It isn't ready to have babies until it's about a hundred fifty.
The Greenland shark. The longest-living animal with a backbone.
Older than your country, and still swimming.
It's also one of the slowest fish ever measured.
I could almost keep up. Almost.
Under one mile an hour.
Yet in its stomach, scientists have found seals.
And even pieces of polar bears and reindeer, probably scavenged.
Many have a little parasite hanging from one eye.
It can grow longer than a car.
Fresh, its meat is poisonous to people.
In Iceland, people ferment it for months, then eat it.
It's called hakarl, and it's famous for its smell.
